title: Single-complex module base change with the pinned tensor counit
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $g:S'\to S$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be scheme morphisms satisfying $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ [def-pc-scheme]. Fix derived module categories [def-pc-derived-category], additive tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], derived pullbacks [def-pc-derived-pullback], and derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and an integer $n$, set $B_n(G)=Lg^*Rf_*(G[-n])$ and $C_n(G)=Rf'_*((g'^*G)[-n])$, where a module shifted by $-n$ is placed in degree $n$. Define the single-complex module base-change composite $\delta^{(n)}_{f,g,g',f'}(G):B_n(G)\to C_n(G)$ to be the recorded derived base-change mate at $G[-n]$ [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], followed by $Rf'_*$ of the composition-pinned comparison $d_{g'}(G,n)$ [def-weil-pbc-pinned-single-degree-tensor-comparison]. The functors $B_n,C_n$ act on coefficient morphisms by these same composites of functors. The mate and the comparison use the same composition-pinned left-derived counit. No cartesian, flatness, properness, affineness, boundedness, or quasi-coherence hypothesis is required.
